A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGA Wasserstein-barycenter work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and additions to Appendix B.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-distribution, 3D-interpolation and surveillance-video experiments, including numerical objectives, runtimes, visual results and an annealing-step experiment in Appendix B.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds residual diagnostics, handwritten-digit results and Gaussian barycenter and transport-map evaluations in Appendix B.2–B.4.

M1.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces SGA-AdaGrad, with accumulated squared gradients and elementwise adaptive updates specified in Algorithm 6. This extends the optimization procedure; the original dual formulation and Algorithms 2–5 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3–B.4 adds handwritten-digit images and truncated two-dimensional Gaussian distributions to the retained shape, 3D and surveillance examples. The Gaussian scenario also evaluates recovery of analytically known barycenters and transport maps, substantially extending empirical coverage.

E2.justification: WDHA, CWB and DSB remain the external comparators, with unchanged membership in the retained experiments. The new digit comparison in Table 4 additionally evaluates SGA-AdaGrad against ordinary SGA and these baselines.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings are retained. New protocols use ten 500×500 digit images and Gaussians discretized on a 1024×1024 grid, introduce squared Wasserstein error against an analytic barycenter and relative squared L2 transport-map errors, and inspect residuals at iterations 100, 200 and 300.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic of the convergence theorem's gradient-bound condition in B.2, an adaptive-versus-constant-step comparison in B.3, and transport-map approximation-error analysis in B.4. These examine additional questions beyond the retained update-scheme and annealing-step analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The new residual measurements at different iterations are trajectory diagnostics, not repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all numerical entries, and the original figure results are preserved. New Tables 3–7 report residual decay, digit performance and Gaussian accuracy. For example, Table 4 gives digit objectives of 5.992×10^-3 for both SGA variants versus 6.049×10^-3 for WDHA; Table 5 gives Gaussian squared Wasserstein errors of 0.4636 for SGA versus 20.3449 for WDHA. These are newly reported settings.

T1.justification: Equation (5) corrects the Poisson forcing from the difference of the input measures to the difference involving the transported measure. Theorem 6 and A.7 correct M to use squared weights and squared residual norms. A.6 also adds the explicit Sobolev-gradient derivation. The principal theorems, convergence rates and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims of a constraint-free concave dual formulation, projection-free SGA and global convergence. However, v2 drops v1's explicit first-in-the-literature guarantee assertions accompanying Theorems 1 and 6, modestly narrowing its stated novelty.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 adds concrete requirements and expected costs for extending SGA to nonuniform grids, and discusses accuracy–scalability tradeoffs of higher-dimensional alternatives. Remark 2 and B.2 newly interpret decreasing residuals as evidence for boundedness and convergence. The original dimensionality limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a statement that simulation code is supplied as supplementary material, AdaGrad hyperparameters, digit specifications, and Gaussian parameters and truncation details. It also identifies FFT-based Poisson solving and discretized pushforwards. Existing hardware and baseline sources remain, while v1's explicit data-license disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and discussion covering neural and regularized barycenters, linear-programming approaches, medical imaging, the digit dataset and nonuniform-grid transforms. These broaden context while retaining the central positioning around exact, constraint-free barycenter computation. The signed-barycenter reference updates an already cited work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include local terminology and explanation edits, author-year citations, reorganization of Theorem 4's presentation, additional Appendix B subsections, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements. Several appendix references now incorrectly call retained lemmas or remarks theorems.

P2.justification: The empirical appendix gains diagnostic and accuracy displays in Tables 3–7, a multi-panel digit comparison in Figure 6, and Algorithm 6. The document also adopts ICLR formatting and relocates existing floats. Figures 1–5 retain identical image content, and Tables 1–2 retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The corrected gradient and convergence formulas improve mathematical consistency, while the new Gaussian ground-truth and map-error checks strengthen validation beyond v1's objective values and visual examples. These provide an incremental overall gain. The benefits are tempered by B.2 overstating what finite residual observations establish about general boundedness and convergence, and by removal of the data-license disclosure.
